canonical_data: in-process team, agent, task, and workflow-log state held in a Redux-style store; persistence is left to the application
strengths: Agents, tasks, and teams are first-class objects, with task results passed between tasks and a team-level memory switch
A subscribable workflow log records task status changes with duration, token usage, and cost details, and the Kaiban Board visualises tasks moving from To Do to Done
Runs in Node.js and in React, Vue, Angular, and Next.js front ends, accepts tools from the wider JavaScript agent ecosystem, and can hand a task to Claude Code, OpenCode, or Codex command lines
weaknesses: The README carries a beta stability badge and the default branch has not been pushed since May 2026
The coding-agent delegation runs through Node child processes and the README says it is intended for local development
Durable storage and recovery of interrupted runs are not documented in the README, so production persistence is left to the application
why_it_matters: A JavaScript-native multi-agent framework with a visual task board, filling the slot that Python frameworks leave open for web-stack teams.
